verdicts.reason: Code matches claim exactly: merge_remote calls repo.merge() at line 291, conflict path does reset+cleanup_state at 308-309, clean path cleanup_state at 330. validate_repo() (94-136) never checks repo.state() or calls cleanup_state, and stage_and_commit's index.write_tree() (231) would indeed hit a not-fully-merged index on a subsequent sync. Mechanism is real as written.

run_loop (69-126) confirmed to have no periodic timer: it blocks on receiver.recv().await (93) then only arms a single debounce sleep once a record arrives; startup_flush call is at line 88. std::mem::take(&mut batch) at line 121 matches, and sync.rs:36 comment text matches verbatim. No guard contradicts the claim.

stage_and_commit only stages paths in the batch loop (216-228), confirmed. has_unpushed/unpushed_count (140-175) only use graph_ahead_behind on commit refs, never inspect working-tree/staged state, confirmed. startup_flush passes Vec::new() at task.rs:88, confirmed. Mechanism accurately described.

merge_remote's dirty check and early return at lines 285-288 match verbatim; the force checkout later in the function (332) would indeed discard uncommitted edits absent that guard, and there is no retry/self-heal path in the cited code.

vault_lock.lock().await at task.rs:149 is correct, and it occurs only after the debounce timer fires, batch is taken (121), and message/paths built (140-146) — a real window during which a new write could land before the lock is acquired. dirty_tracked_files (sync.rs:338) would then see that file as WT_MODIFIED during the current batch's merge check. Nothing in the cited files contradicts this race.

Confirmed under failure-injection: repo.merge() (git2) writes the merge result (including conflict entries, if any) to the on-disk index and sets MERGE_HEAD/RepositoryState::Merge as part of the call itself, before this function's conflict-check/cleanup_state at 308-309 or the clean-path commit/cleanup_state at 319-330 ever runs. A kill between 291 and either cleanup point leaves MERGE_HEAD and a (possibly conflicted) index persisted on disk. Nothing in this file inspects repo.state() or calls cleanup_state()/reset at startup or at the top of sync()/stage_and_commit() -- validate_repo() only checks workdir/HEAD/remote. On the next sync, stage_and_commit() reopens that same on-disk index (215) and calls index.write_tree() (231), which libgit2 rejects (GIT_EUNMERGED) whenever the persisted index still has unresolved conflict stages -- exactly the case left behind by a crash after a conflicting merge but before the abort-reset at 307-309. That produces a permanent GitError::Other on every subsequent sync with no self-healing code path in this module, matching the finding. (For the narrower sub-case where the crash lands during an already-clean, conflict-free merge but before the final commit/cleanup_state at 330, write_tree itself may still succeed, so 'every' failure is slightly overstated for that one sub-window, but the central claim -- an unrecovered crash-mid-merge wedges the repo with no auto-recovery in this file -- holds.)

No guard exists in sync.rs: validate_repo() never checks repo.state() nor calls cleanup_state()/merge-abort, and stage_and_commit() unconditionally calls index.write_tree() on the on-disk index every sync (including the very next one after a crash) before any merge logic runs. If the crash lands after repo.merge() (which persists MERGE_HEAD/conflicted index to disk as part of the call) but before the conflict-path reset+cleanup_state (308-309) or the clean-path cleanup_state (330), the wedge is real and self-inflicted on every subsequent sync attempt, with recovery only via manual `git merge --abort`. No upstream crate or existing code path mitigates this; severity as a durability/availability issue for the sync subsystem is not overstated.
